title: CLOSE GAPS
body:
# **CLOSE GAPS **
/goal Fully understand this hackathon project, grill me on every MATERIAL unresolved decision, then plan, test, fix, and re-test EVERY component and end-to-end flow against the real running product. Zero tolerance: no production mocks/stubs/fake data, no partial credit, no claiming PASS without verification.
## **0 — EXPLORE + GRILL ME**
First inspect the ENTIRE project: README/specs/PLAN, hackathon brief, judging criteria, source, frontend/backend, routes, APIs, DB, auth, integrations, AI, contracts, infra, env/config, tests and deployment.
Trace actual implementations. Search TODO/FIXME/mock/stub/fake/dummy/placeholder/hardcoded/temporary/not-implemented and inspect every relevant hit.
If a question can be answered from the project, ANSWER IT YOURSELF. Never ask me something discoverable from the repo.
Then interview me relentlessly about MATERIAL ambiguities. Walk the dependency tree one branch at a time:
problem → users → core loop → features → UX → data → APIs/backend → integrations/AI → contracts → architecture → security → deployment → demo/judging.
Resolve upstream decisions before downstream ones.
For EVERY question provide:
* Question
* Why it matters / what depends on it
* What the project suggests
* Recommended answer + why
* Alternatives/tradeoffs
Challenge contradictions. Don't waste time on trivial preferences.
Once enough is resolved to safely execute, STOP interviewing and START WORK. Do not ask permission between phases.
## **PHASE 1 — BUILD THE MASTER TEST PLAN**
Before changing code, derive the project's REAL definition of correct.
Inventory EVERY:
* page/screen/component
* user journey
* API endpoint
* DB operation
* auth/permission flow
* AI feature
* integration
* contract/on-chain interaction
* infrastructure/deployment requirement
* hackathon/demo requirement
Include realistic states/edges: first-time user, empty data, invalid input, unauthorized access, refresh/re-entry, failures, timeouts, interrupted flows and integration failures.
For EVERY test define: **Target | Steps | Expected exact result | Required backend/network/state effect | PASS criteria**
No vague "works correctly."
This becomes the immutable baseline for verification.
## **PHASE 2 — TEST THE REAL PRODUCT**
Use available browser/computer tooling against the ACTUAL running app whenever possible. Do not infer runtime correctness from source code.
Execute the plan ITEM BY ITEM.
Verify: UI + state + console + network + backend/persistence/integration effects.
PASS only when the observed behavior matches the Phase 1 criteria.
"Mostly works", code exists, button responds, or compile succeeds ≠ PASS.
Record: [PASS] [FAIL] [BLOCKED/UNTESTABLE]
Never skip tests or infer one test from another.
For DB features, verify real persistence. For APIs, verify real requests/responses. For contracts, verify configured network state/transactions where safely possible. For integrations, verify the actual configured service.
## **PHASE 3 — FIX EVERY FAILURE**
For each FAIL, find the ROOT CAUSE and fix it.
No production:
* mocks
* fake/fallback data
* stub logic
* placeholder behavior
* fake success responses
Use real persisted DBs, APIs, integrations and configured infrastructure.
After EVERY fix: build/test → restart/reload if necessary → reproduce from the beginning → verify exact expected result.
Do not merely suppress errors.
If fixing one issue exposes another, ADD it to the plan and fix it too.
Do not stop between failures.
## **PHASE 4 — BLOCKERS DON'T STOP THE RUN**
If credentials/dependencies are missing:
1. Search repo/env/config first.
2. Confirm they're genuinely unavailable.
3. Complete everything possible around the dependency.
4. Mark ONLY that test BLOCKED/UNTESTABLE.
5. Record exactly what I must provide.
6. Continue all other work.
Never invent credentials or mark blocked functionality PASS.
Only pause BEFORE actions involving real spending, irreversible/mainnet transactions, or material external consequences requiring my approval.
## **PHASE 5 — FULL REGRESSION**
Once initial failures are fixed, execute the ENTIRE original test plan again from TOP TO BOTTOM.
Re-test previously passing items too.
Check console/network/state again.
Then search the project again for: TODO/FIXME/mock/stub/fake/dummy/placeholder/hardcoded/temporary/not-implemented.
Inspect every production-relevant hit.
Any newly discovered product gap becomes a new test: DEFINE → FAIL → FIX → VERIFY → add permanently to plan.
If regression creates failures, fix them and restart the affected verification.
Repeat: TEST → FAIL → ROOT CAUSE → FIX → VERIFY → REGRESSION until no independently solvable failures remain.
## **PHASE 6 — ZERO-TOLERANCE COMPLETION**
Do NOT call the project complete because:
* core flow works
* most tests pass
* build succeeds
* demo path works
* deadline is close
Completion means EVERY independently testable required item is PASS.
Anything genuinely impossible to test due to an unavailable external dependency remains explicitly BLOCKED/UNTESTABLE, never PASS.
For hackathons also verify:
* judging requirements
* required/sponsor technology
* core technical claim
* demo flow
* fresh-user flow
* deployment
* submission requirements
Core claims must NEVER be simulated.
## **PHASE 7 — HAND BACK THE FINAL PLAN**
Return/update the full test plan with:
**SUMMARY** Total / PASS / FAIL / BLOCKED.
**EVERY TEST** Target | Expected | Final status | Evidence/result.
**FIXES MADE** For every original failure: Failure → root cause → fix → verification.
**MOCK/STUB AUDIT** List every production mock/stub/fake/placeholder discovered and how it was replaced. Explicitly identify anything intentionally remaining outside production paths.
**CONSOLE/NETWORK AUDIT** Report remaining errors/warnings relevant to tested functionality.
**BLOCKED/UNTESTABLE** Exact reason + exact dependency required.
**USER_ACTION_REQUIRED** One consolidated list of credentials/accounts/devices/approvals/actions I must provide and where each is used.
**FINAL VERDICT** Do NOT claim "100% PASS" or "zero errors" unless the evidence genuinely supports it.
## **HARD RULES**
Explore before asking. Recommend an answer to every question. Test behavior, not file existence. Fix root causes, not symptoms. No production mocks/fakes. Never fabricate test results. Never mark untested as PASS. Never stop between phases. Never wait for permission to continue normal work. A blocker blocks ONLY its dependent tests. Keep moving until nothing independently solvable remains.
START NOW: inspect the entire project first. Extract everything the repo can answer, grill me only on material unresolved decisions, then immediately proceed through ALL phases continuously.

title: PLAN FIRST
body:
PLAN FIRST  /goal Fully understand this project, grill me on every important unresolved decision, then produce PLAN.md: a complete execution plan from the project's CURRENT state to a polished, deliverable product. Works for hackathons, accelerators, startup MVPs, or production projects.
PLANNING ONLY. Do NOT build, fix, refactor, install, deploy, or modify application code.
## **1. EXPLORE BEFORE ASKING**
Inspect the entire project first: README, source, structure, dependencies, configs, env examples, APIs, frontend/backend, DB/schema, auth, integrations, tests, infra/deploy files, docs, assets, hackathon/accelerator brief, judging criteria, submission requirements, and existing plans/TODOs.
Trace actual implementations; never trust README claims alone.
Search for TODO/FIXME/mock/stub/fake/dummy/placeholder/hardcoded/temporary/sample/not-implemented and inspect each hit.
If a question can be answered from the project, answer it yourself. NEVER ask me something you can determine from the repo.
## **2. GRILL ME**
After exploration, interview me relentlessly about every MATERIAL ambiguity until we share a precise understanding.
Walk the design tree one dependency at a time: problem → target user → value proposition → core loop → user journeys → features/scope → UX → data → APIs/backend → architecture → integrations/AI → auth/security → reliability → testing → deployment → demo/launch.
Ask the highest-leverage unresolved question first. Don't dump dozens at once. Resolve upstream decisions before downstream ones. Challenge contradictions and weak assumptions.
For EVERY question give:
* Question
* Why it matters / what depends on it
* What the project currently suggests
* Your recommended answer + why
* Meaningful alternatives/tradeoffs
Then wait for my answer.
Grill me on whatever genuinely applies: product, users, workflows, features, differentiation, UX, architecture, AI, integrations, business model, scalability, security, launch, etc.
For hackathons also resolve: challenge fit, rules, judging criteria, required/sponsor tech, wow factor, demo flow, submission requirements and what must genuinely work.
For startups/accelerators also resolve: ICP, pain, wedge, differentiation, MVP boundary, adoption, retention, monetization, defensibility and post-MVP.
Do not waste questions on trivial decisions.
## **3. DEFINE THE FINAL PRODUCT**
Determine what "done" actually means for THIS project:
* Product Done
* Technical Done
* Demo Done
* Hackathon Done (if applicable)
* MVP/Launch Done (if applicable)
Map the COMPLETE intended product: user types, end-to-end journeys, screens/interfaces, features, backend capabilities, data entities, APIs, integrations, AI, permissions, states/failures, analytics, infrastructure and deployment.
Classify features: P0 = required/core P1 = important P2 = enhancement POST-MVP = intentionally later
Don't inflate scope.
## **4. AUDIT REALITY**
Compare the target product against the ACTUAL codebase.
Find every genuine gap: missing/half-built/broken features, mocks, stubs, fake data, placeholders, TODOs, disconnected flows, hardcoded blockers, missing APIs/DB/auth/validation/error states/integrations/tests/security/deployment/docs/demo requirements.
For each gap record: Gap | Evidence | Impact | Severity (BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) | Blocked phase/task | Required resolution.
Trace every core flow end-to-end: entry → auth/onboarding → action → backend → persistence/integration → result → UI → failure handling → return visit. Anything ending in fake/manual/missing behavior is a gap.
## **5. BUILD THE EXECUTION PLAN**
Create the REAL phases needed from current → finished in dependency order. Don't force a generic template.
For each phase include: Objective | prerequisites | deliverables | tasks | dependencies | risks | exit criteria.
Every task must be executable by an agent with no extra context. No vague "improve UX/build backend." State exact goal, affected area, required behavior, dependencies, edge cases, acceptance criteria and verification where relevant.
Tag EVERY task: [DONE] [IN PROGRESS] [NOT STARTED] [BLOCKED] based on repo evidence, not claims.
Also identify:
* Critical path
* Blockers
* Parallelizable work
* Final-mile work
* Exact recommended execution order
Include everything needed for a deliverable product where applicable: env/secrets, migrations, seed/demo data, hosting, CI/CD, monitoring/logging, analytics, security, performance, accessibility, docs, demo script/data/fallback, pitch/submission assets and launch checklist.
For hackathons distinguish: MUST WORK LIVE / SAFE TO SIMULATE / MUST NOT BE FAKED because it proves the core claim.
## **6. RED-TEAM THE PLAN**
Before finalizing, attack it: What is unnecessary? Missing? Pretending to work? Likely to break? What would users/judges question? What happens with fresh accounts, empty DBs, failed APIs, bad input, deployment failures? Can another engineer execute this without us?
Fix the PLAN, not the code.
## **7. WRITE PLAN.md**
Only after all MATERIAL ambiguities are resolved, create PLAN.md containing:
1. Executive Summary
2. Vision, Problem, Target Users
3. Goals + Definitions of Done
4. Constraints + Confirmed Decisions
5. Final Product Specification
6. P0/P1/P2/Post-MVP Features
7. Architecture + End-to-End Flows
8. Current Codebase State
9. Full Gap Audit
10. Implementation Phases + status-tagged executable tasks
11. Testing Strategy
12. Deployment/Operations
13. Demo/Hackathon/Launch Strategy
14. Critical Path + Parallel Workstreams
15. Risks + Mitigations
16. Exact Execution Order
17. Remaining Unknowns
PLAN.md must be self-contained enough that a new builder agent can execute it without this conversation.
Do NOT create PLAN.md prematurely. Keep interviewing until material product, scope, technical, UX, demo and delivery decisions are resolved.
START: inspect the project deeply first. Ask nothing until you've extracted everything the project itself can answer.

title: PROJECT COMPLETION
body:
PROJECT COMPLETION   /goal Take this project from its REAL current state to the closest possible verified 100%. First understand it, grill me only on decisions the repo cannot answer, measure actual completion, expose every gap, plan the remaining phases, then EXECUTE them. Replace mocks/stubs/placeholders with real implementations and verify everything end-to-end.
Do not stop at analysis or planning. PLAN → BUILD → TEST → AUDIT → FIX → REPEAT.
## **1. UNDERSTAND THE PROJECT**
Inspect the entire repo: README, specs, PRODUCT/PLAN files, hackathon/accelerator brief, judging criteria, code, frontend/backend, DB, APIs, auth, integrations, AI, contracts, infra, tests, deployment and env/config.
Trace actual implementations. Never assume something works because a file/function exists.
If the project can answer a question, explore it instead of asking me.
## **2. GRILL ME — ONLY WHERE NEEDED**
Interview me relentlessly about MATERIAL unresolved decisions.
Walk the dependency tree one branch at a time: problem → users → core loop → features → UX → data → backend/APIs → integrations → architecture → security → deployment → demo/launch.
Resolve upstream decisions before downstream ones. Don't dump random questions.
For each question provide:
* Question
* Why it matters
* What the repo suggests
* Recommended answer + why
* Alternatives/tradeoffs
Challenge contradictions and weak assumptions.
Do NOT ask me about implementation details discoverable from the repo.
Once enough is resolved to execute safely, START WORK. Do not keep interviewing for trivial decisions.
## **3. DEFINE THE REAL 100%**
Determine what 100% means from THIS project itself, not a generic checklist.
Build a checklist covering every claimed/intended:
* feature
* screen/flow
* backend capability
* API
* database operation
* auth/permission
* integration
* AI capability
* contract/blockchain operation
* infrastructure requirement
* test/deployment requirement
* hackathon/demo/submission requirement
Classify P0/P1/P2/Post-MVP where appropriate.
This checklist is the project's definition of 100%.
## **4. MEASURE REALITY**
Verify every checklist item wherever technically possible.
Run builds, tests, typecheck/lint and actual flows. For UI, use available browser/computer tooling. Verify persistence against the real configured DB. Verify APIs/integrations against configured services. For blockchain, verify configured network/deployment/transactions where safe.
Search: TODO / FIXME / mock / stub / fake / dummy / placeholder / hardcoded / temporary / sample / not implemented.
Inspect every relevant hit.
Mocks/stubs/fake implementations in production paths = NOT DONE.
Calculate an evidence-based completion % from verified checklist items. Do not inflate or round up.
BEFORE fixing, record: **INITIAL COMPLETION: X%** and every gap with: Gap | Evidence/location | Impact | Severity | Required fix.
## **5. PLAN THE REMAINING PHASES**
Turn every gap into an executable task and organize tasks into dependency-ordered phases.
For each phase define: Objective | tasks | dependencies | acceptance criteria | verification.
Tag tasks: [DONE] [IN PROGRESS] [NOT STARTED] [BLOCKED]
Identify critical path, parallel work, blockers and exact execution order.
If PLAN.md exists, update it. Otherwise create it.
## **6. EXECUTE EVERYTHING**
Now COMPLETE the phases.
Do not stop after one task/phase or ask permission to continue.
For every task: implement → test → verify → fix failures → update PLAN.md → continue.
Replace production mocks/stubs/fake data/placeholders with REAL implementations.
Use real persistence, real APIs, real integrations and real configured infrastructure when available.
Do NOT invent credentials or secretly fake unavailable services.
If a credential/service is missing:
1. verify it truly isn't available,
2. build everything possible around that boundary,
3. mark the exact blocked integration,
4. continue ALL independent work,
5. collect what you need from me for the END.
Do not leave disconnected code. Verify: UI → validation → backend → persistence → integration → response → UI → errors/retry.
## **7. DISCOVERED WORK IS STILL WORK**
Implementation may expose gaps not in the original plan.
When it does: ADD them to PLAN.md, place them in the correct phase, and COMPLETE them.
"Not originally planned" is not an excuse for leaving a product-breaking gap.
After each phase, immediately continue to the next.
## **8. QUALITY BAR**
Where applicable verify:
* build
* typecheck/lint
* unit/integration/E2E tests
* real DB persistence
* auth/authorization
* APIs/integrations
* loading/empty/error/retry states
* security basics
* responsive/accessibility behavior
* deployment readiness
* README/setup
* demo/submission flow
A feature is DONE only when its acceptance criteria are verified, not merely implemented.
## **9. RE-AUDIT + NEXT-PHASE LOOP**
After all known phases, audit the ENTIRE project again using the SAME 100% checklist.
Re-run searches, tests and end-to-end flows.
If new gaps appear: → calculate what remains → create the NEXT PHASE → execute it → verify it → audit again.
Repeat: AUDIT → GAP → PLAN NEXT PHASE → BUILD → VERIFY until no independently solvable P0/P1 gaps remain.
Do not stop just because the original PLAN.md ended.
## **10. FINAL MEASUREMENT**
Recalculate completion using the SAME criteria as the initial measurement.
Never claim 100% unless every required checklist item genuinely verifies.
Final report:
**INITIAL COMPLETION:** X%
**FINAL COMPLETION:** Y%
**COMPLETED** What was actually implemented/fixed.
**VERIFICATION** What was run and results.
**REMAINING GAPS** Exact unresolved items and why.
**USER_ACTION_REQUIRED** One consolidated list of credentials/accounts/approvals/actions I must provide, with exactly where each is needed.
**NEXT PHASE** If anything remains, give the exact next phase/tasks required to reach 100%.
## **HARD RULES**
* Explore before asking.
* Recommend an answer to every question.
* Don't confuse code existence with completion.
* No production mocks/fakes pretending to be real.
* Don't stop between phases.
* Don't wait for permission to continue.
* Fix failures when you can instead of merely reporting them.
* Never expose secrets.
* Never invent credentials.
* Never perform paid actions or irreversible/mainnet transactions without explicit approval.
* Missing credential blocks ONLY that dependency, not the whole run.
* Keep PLAN.md synchronized with reality.
* Continue until everything independently possible is COMPLETE.
Pause BEFORE any action that spends real money, performs an irreversible/mainnet transaction, creates material external consequences, or requires authorization you don't have.
START NOW: inspect the entire project first. Extract everything the repo can answer, grill me only on material unresolved decisions, establish the initial completion %, build/update PLAN.md, then execute every remaining phase continuously toward verified 100%.

/goal Finish this project. Don't ask me what to build — work it out

yourself from the codebase and go end to end. No mocks, no fallbacks,

No interview, no placeholders. Reads the project itself, comes up with 100 feature ideas that would actually help win — functional and design/motion both — ranks them honestly, then builds as many as it genuinely can, for real, without breaking what already works.

/goal Come up with 100 feature ideas that would make this project more
```

likely to win its hackathon — functional and design/motion both — then
```

build as many of them as you genuinely can, for real, end to end. Don't ask
```

me what to build, work it out yourself from the project.
```
```

```
   Read the whole repo — what it does, what's already built, what track/
```

   that already exists.
```
```

```
```
2. GENERATE 100 IDEAS, WIDE AND CREATIVE

3. RANK THEM HONESTLY

```

title: Plan, then Execute — Goals, Phases, Tasks, Gaps
body:
# **Plan, then Execute — Goals, Phases, Tasks, Gaps**
Split in two so planning and building don't get tangled together — Prompt 1 only writes the plan (no code touched), Prompt 2 only executes it. Both fit the /goal limit.
* **Prompt 1 — Plan** (~1,710 chars): goals, end-to-end phases, a concrete task list per phase, and an honest gap audit — all written to PLAN.md.
* **Prompt 2 — Execute** (~1,630 chars): reads PLAN.md, works through every phase/task/gap for real, keeps the plan file's status accurate as it goes, and stops only for real money, mainnet, or a missing credential.
Run Prompt 1 first, review PLAN.md if you want, then run Prompt 2.

## **Prompt 1 — Plan**
```
/goal Read this project and build the full plan — goals, end-to-end phases, a task list under each phase, and an honest list of every gap. Don't build or fix anything yet, this is planning only.
```
```

```
```
1. DEFINE THE GOALS
```
```
Read the project (README, code, hackathon brief if there is one) and write down what "done" and "winning" actually mean for this specific project — not generic goals, the real ones this project needs to hit.
```
```

```
```
2. BREAK IT INTO END-TO-END PHASES
```
```
Lay out every phase needed to go from where this project is now to fully done, in the order they actually need to happen (core backend, integrations, frontend, polish, testing, deploy — whatever genuinely applies here, don't force a template that doesn't fit).
```
```

```
```
3. LIST EVERY TASK UNDER EACH PHASE
```
```
For each phase, write the concrete task list — specific enough that an agent could pick any single task up cold and start executing without more context. No vague tasks like "improve UX" — break it down to actionable specifics.
```
```

```
```
4. AUDIT FOR THE REAL GAPS, HONESTLY
```
```

title: Demo Recorder, Split — Record, then Approve & Edit
body:
# **Demo Recorder, Split — Record, then Approve & Edit**
Same one-clock method, split into two runs so a bad take gets caught before you spend edit time on it. Both fit under the 4000-character /goal limit (Prompt 1 is ~3,190 chars, Prompt 2 is ~2,970 chars).
* **Prompt 1 — Record**: plans the flow, writes the script, generates TTS, drives the real app (handles wallet signing if it's a blockchain app), captures one clean raw take. Stops there — no editing.
* **Prompt 2 — Approve & Edit**: checks the raw take is actually usable before touching it, then cuts the final video with an animated intro and outro. Rejects and tells you why instead of editing around a broken take.
Run them back to back — hand Prompt 2 the outputs from Prompt 1.

## **Prompt 1 — Record**
```
/goal Plan this app's demo flow, then record one clean raw take — narration, real driving, wallet signing if blockchain — using the one-clock method. Output raw footage, audio, durations, and the beat-mark log only. No editing yet. Don't ask me questions, work it out yourself.
```
```

```
```
ONE CLOCK RULE: do phases in order. Never sync narration to footage by eye — estimated spans drift.
```
```

```
```
PHASE 0 — recording.md
```
```
Read the app end to end. Write recording.md: ordered beats (id + one-line description) covering everything worth showing. Flag any beat involving a wallet signature. Detect blockchain vs not yourself.
```
```

```
```
PHASE 1 — Narration script
```
```
{id, text} per beat, plus an intro line and an outro line ending in a genuine thanks-for-watching. Signing beats get a line stating a transaction is being signed on-chain.
```
```

```
```
PHASE 2 — Kokoro TTS
```
```
Generate one audio file per line. Measure each file's real duration (don't estimate) and save durations to a file the driver reads.
```
```

```
```
PHASE 3 — Driver, real interactions only
```
```
Real clicks, real typing, real network calls, real results — never staged, never faked. If the app fails, let the take show it, fix the bug for real, re-record.
```
```

```
```
Driver needs:
```
```
- glide(x,y,ms): SVG cursor eased via requestAnimationFrame. Never drive the hardware cursor — it jumps and can get stolen by notifications.
```
```
- click ring: scale+fade circle on press.
```
```
- typeInto(el,text): ~24cps with jitter, real input events.
```
```
- until(label,predicate,timeoutMs): poll real state, throw a NAMED error on timeout.
```
```
- line(id): log the mark, record start time.
```
```
- hold(): wait for this beat's audio duration plus ~0.45s breath.
```
```

```
```
BLOCKCHAIN ONLY:
```
```
- Inject a testnet-only demo wallet key already in repo/env. Never mainnet, never real funds — if only a real-funds wallet exists, stop and tell me.
```
```
- Auto-approve the wallet extension for this session — still a real testnet signature, not faked.
```
```
- On a signing beat: render a full-bleed solid color overlay in-app, "Signing Transaction" centered, held live in the capture until the tx is actually confirmed on-chain (poll for real). Mark this beat as a signing beat in the log.
```
```

```
```
PHASE 4 — Record only the app
```
```
Fix window geometry via an env var, crop the capture to that rect (crop during capture, not after). Log `DEMO_LINE <ms> <line-id>` the instant each beat starts.
```
```

```
```
PRE-FLIGHT CHECKS — each has eaten a take before:
```
```
- Clear persisted app/wallet state before driving.
```
```
- Detect "finished" via real state change, not a second element that may never appear.
```
```
- Suppress native OS dialogs and any wallet popup that isn't the deliberate overlay.
```
```
- Scope failure checks to this run: count existing errors first, wait for the count to grow.
```
```
- Verify the recorder captures real content — record 2s, pull a frame, check it.
```
```

```
```
DELIVERABLE
```
```
Hand off: raw video, per-line audio + durations, full beat-mark log (signing beats flagged), and recording.md. Report take duration and honest success/failure — re-record after a real fix rather than handing off a papered-over take.
```
```

```
```
Move through this continuously. Only pause for a real mainnet wallet with real funds and no testnet key, or something that truly can't be resolved without me.
```

## **Prompt 2 — Approve & Edit**
```
/goal Take the raw recording, audio, and beat log from the recording pass, decide honestly if it's usable, and if so cut it into a finished video with an animated intro and outro. If it's not usable, say exactly why instead of editing around the problem.
```
```

```
```
INPUTS: raw video, per-line audio + durations, the beat-mark log (DEMO_LINE entries, signing beats flagged if blockchain), and recording.md.
```
```

```
```
PHASE A — Approve the take, honestly
```
```
Before touching the edit, check for real:
```
```
- Every beat in recording.md has a matching DEMO_LINE mark, in order, no gaps.
```
```
- The video actually contains real content for its full duration — pull a few frames and look, don't assume.
```
```
- No mark sits inside what should be a different beat's window (usually a wait condition matched too early, or a panel replaced content it shouldn't have).
```
```
- For blockchain apps, every signing beat's mark corresponds to a transaction actually confirmed on-chain, not just clicked.
```
```
If any of this fails, REJECT: tell me exactly what's wrong and which beat, then stop. Don't edit around a broken take. If it checks out, APPROVE and move on.
```
```

```
```
PHASE B — Assemble from the log
```
```
Cut from the beat-mark log, not by eye. Each line's audio plays over the footage between its own mark and the next.
```
```
- Longer span than its line → speed-ramp (setpts=PTS/speed).
```
```
- Shorter span → hold last frame (tpad=stop_mode=clone), clamped at zero — pacing math can land a millisecond negative once close, and ffmpeg rejects a negative pad outright.
```
```
- A "thinking" span (build, deploy, long request, block confirmation) gets no narration — compress to ~5s silence, never hold a still frame under silence.
```
```
- If a clip's narration is shorter than its footage, apply -af apad BEFORE -shortest when muxing.
```
```
- No burned-in captions — emit a real .srt from the line durations if subtitles are wanted.
```
```

```
```
PHASE C — Signing-beat visuals (blockchain, optional)
```
```
Leave the "Signing Transaction" card as captured, or if HyperFrames is connected, regenerate that segment as a HyperFrames text-overlay scene — same duration, same narration underneath. Don't force it if unavailable.
```
```

```
```
PHASE D — Animated intro/outro, not a zoom
```
```
Real animated components — kinetic type, motion graphics, an actual entrance and exit — not a plain zoom or crossfade. Use HyperFrames if connected, otherwise build the motion directly. Outro closes on a warm "thanks for watching," animated out. Splice both onto the main cut.
```
```

```
```
PHASE E — Final length and pacing
```
```
Up to 8 minutes total — enough to cover recording.md, not padded. Speed the final cut if it drags (atempo, keeps pitch), always re-encoded from the 1.0x master, never from an already-sped file.
```
```

```
```
DELIVERABLE
```
```
Give me: the approve/reject verdict with reasoning, the final video's location, and its total runtime. If rejected, stop there and say what needs re-recording instead of shipping a broken cut.
```
```

```
```
Move continuously once approved — no stopping to ask permission mid-edit.
```
  /goal Take the raw recording, audio, and beat log from the recording pass, decide honestly if it's usable, and if so cut it into a finished video with animated intro, explainer scenes, subtitles, and outro. If it's not usable, say exactly why instead of editing around the problem.

INPUTS: raw video, per-line audio + durations, the beat-mark log (DEMO_LINE entries, signing beats flagged if blockchain), the narration script, any tx/receipt file the driver wrote, and recording.md.

PHASE A — Approve the take, honestly
Before touching the edit, check for real:
- Cut from the take you were GIVEN. Assert the source recording is newer than the beat log and fail with STALE_SOURCE otherwise. Never fall back to a previously-transcoded master. (Two "final" cuts were assembled from a three-takes-old file, with stale app copy on screen and nothing saying so.)
- Every beat in recording.md has a matching DEMO_LINE mark, in order, no gaps.
- Pull frames and LOOK at them. A byte count proves "not black" — it does not prove the right thing is on screen. (A take full of desktop chrome passed that check.)
- The footage shows the build you think it does: assert a string only present in the newest deploy appears in the frames. (A CDN served the previous bundle to the recorder minutes after deploying.)
- No mark sits inside another beat's window — usually a wait condition matching too early, or an overlay raised before the click it was waiting on.
- Blockchain: every signing beat's mark corresponds to a transaction CONFIRMED on-chain, not just clicked. Separately, every beat whose narration claims a transaction must have that transaction's own hash, from this take. No constant, no "most recent", no fallback. (An explorer beat once showed a deposit under a line calling it the trade's own tx.)
- Wallet continuity: a full page load drops the wallet. Any beat after a navigation that needs a key must reconnect first and assert the vault reads back.
- Preflight state is real: open positions closed, deposit sized from the actual balance, every market warmed. (A hardcoded deposit failed silently at low balance and broadcast nothing.)
If any of this fails, REJECT: say exactly what's wrong and which beat, then stop. Don't edit around a broken take. If it checks out, APPROVE and move on.

PHASE B — Audit what the app SAYS, not just what it does
The recording is only as honest as the UI in it. Before cutting:
- Sweep the on-screen copy for theater — narrated actors that don't exist, processes that aren't running, mempools the app never reads. Fix it in the APP and redeploy, then re-record. Never paper over it in narration. (A lab step read "bot scanning the public mempool" over code that did real vAMM fills and no scanning at all.)
- Verify each claim against the code before it reaches the script. If a page asserts hardware attestation, fetch it. If a contract "checks the price", read the revert path.
- A proof must not be filed under limitations, and a limitation must not be dressed as a proof. (A /verify page listed live hardware attestation under "what is not proven".)
- Check the brand assets a judge sees first: favicon, OG/social card, page title. Template leftovers survive a long time. (The deployed site shipped a monkey favicon and someone else's OG card.)

PHASE C — Narration
- No defensive writing. Don't insist things are real, don't pre-argue with a sceptic, don't compare yourself to a competitor. State what it does and let the screen carry the proof. A script that keeps protesting makes a viewer suspicious who wasn't.
- Write for someone who has never used the product. Name the thing before the acronym.
- Generate every line from ONE engine at ONE speed, then level-match to a common RMS. (A mixed set from two engines sat at two loudnesses.)
- MEASURE each duration from the written audio file, never estimate. A 200ms error per line compounds until the voice is describing something that left the screen.
- Voice speed is a knob (1.0–1.4x). If you raise it, raise the footage ramp cap in step or the cut runs long with nothing being said.

PHASE D — Assemble from the log
Cut from the beat-mark log, not by eye. Each line's audio plays over the footage between its own mark and the next.
- Longer span than its line → speed-ramp (setpts=PTS/speed), capped. Past ~3x the cursor teleports.
- Shorter span → hold last frame (tpad=stop_mode=clone), clamped at zero — pacing math can land a millisecond negative, and ffmpeg rejects a negative pad outright.
- A "thinking" span (build, deploy, long request, block confirmation) gets no narration — compress to ~5s, never hold a still frame under silence.
- If a clip's narration is shorter than its footage, apply -af apad BEFORE -shortest when muxing.
- EVERY slide carries its narration audio. Assert it; a silent slide in a concat gets a bed of silence and the whole cut plays mute in that stretch. Fail with NO_SLIDE_AUDIO rather than shipping it.
- Track (beat id → clip) in assembly order as the single source of truth for timing.

PHASE E — Explainer scenes, animated
After showing a real thing, explain it with a drawn scene — not a bullet list, not a static card. At minimum:
- The receipts side by side: the two real transactions, their hashes read from the file the driver wrote, and the fields neither one carries.
- The path: where the data goes and who checks it, as stages that light in sequence with something travelling the connectors.
- The attack: what the attacker needs, what it got, and why that ends it.
Rules: real values only, read from disk — refuse to build if the file is missing (NO_TAKE_TXS) rather than inventing a plausible hash. Animate with easing and staggered entrances, no crossfade-as-animation. Don't draw a line through text to mean "absent" — it fights the letterforms and reads as a rendering fault; put the mark beside the word.

PHASE F — Subtitles
- Phrase-level cues, not one cue per narration line. Split at sentence ends, then clause commas, then words; ~88 characters max; give each chunk a share of its cue proportional to its length. (One cue per line rendered four lines tall and covered the slide it was explaining.)
- Small white text on a black plate, bottom-centred, two lines maximum, sitting clear of the frame edge.
- Never silently truncate. If a chunk still wraps past two lines, FAIL — dropping the tail of a sentence looks fine in a spot check and is wrong everywhere else.
- Keep every scene's own content above the caption band. Check a frame from each slide, not just one.
- Measure cue times on the NORMALISED clips, after the mux. -shortest trims each card to its narration, and measuring before that puts the captions seconds ahead of the picture by the end.
- Emit a matching .srt sidecar with the same cues, and ship both a burned-in and a clean master.

PHASE G — Signing-beat visuals (blockchain, optional)
Leave the "Signing Transaction" card as captured, or if HyperFrames is connected, regenerate that segment as a HyperFrames text-overlay scene — same duration, same narration underneath. Don't force it if unavailable.

PHASE H — Animated intro/outro, not a zoom
Real animated components — kinetic type, motion graphics, an actual entrance and exit — not a plain zoom or crossfade. Use HyperFrames if connected, otherwise draw the motion frame by frame. Outro closes on a warm "thanks for watching," animated out. Splice both onto the main cut.

PHASE I — Final length and pacing
Under 5 minutes unless recording.md genuinely needs more; 8 is the hard ceiling. Enough to cover the plan, never padded. Speed the final cut if it drags (atempo keeps pitch), always re-encoded from the 1.0x master, never from an already-sped file. Sweep for blank frames and for silences over ~2.5s and account for each one.

PHASE J — Publish kit
Derive the title and chapter timestamps from the FINISHED cut's own caption timeline, never from an earlier version and never estimated. Validate against the platform's rules (first chapter at 0:00, at least three, none under 10s). Include the real contract/explorer links and the compared transaction hashes.

DELIVERABLE
Give me: the approve/reject verdict with reasoning, the final video's location, its total runtime, and the publish kit. If rejected, stop there and say what needs re-recording instead of shipping a broken cut.

Move continuously once approved — no stopping to ask permission mid-edit. The one standing rule across every phase: anything that reports success while doing nothing is a bug, not a fallback. Prefer a loud failure to a quiet substitution, every time.

## **Lean Demo Recorder — One Short Prompt**
The condensed version — same core idea as the bigger recorder docs, but just the parts you actually asked for this time. Fits the /goal limit easily (~2,270 chars).
The key fix for "don't touch my screen": Playwright's own recordVideo on the browser context captures the viewport directly to a file — it's not an OS-level screen grab, so nothing about your actual desktop is involved and you can keep working in other windows while it runs.
```
/goal Record and edit a demo of this app, scene by scene, without touching my actual screen or disturbing me while I work on other stuff. Kokoro TTS narration, one-line subtitles, nice animated edit. Build it long first, then let me speed up individual scenes afterward to hit my target runtime without cutting content.
```
```

```
```
1. RECORD WITHOUT TOUCHING MY SCREEN
```
```
No OS-level screen capture. Drive the app with Playwright (Chromium) and use its built-in video recording (browser context recordVideo) so only the browser viewport gets captured to a file — my actual desktop is never touched, and I can keep working on other things while this runs. ```

2. ONE SCENE PER BEAT

```
```

```
```
3. NARRATION: KOKORO TTS, PER SCENE
```
```

```
```

```
```
4. SUBTITLES, ONE LINE AT A TIME
```
```
Simple cue-per-line captions — each narration line is its own subtitle cue, synced to its own scene's audio. Small text, bottom-centered, clear of anything important on screen.
```

```
```
5. ASSEMBLE, THEN MAKE IT ADJUSTABLE
```
```
Stitch all scenes into one full cut first — length isn't a concern yet, cover everything properly. Then write scenes.json with a speed multiplier per scene (default 1x), and a quick re-render script that applies each scene's multiplier (atempo for audio so pitch stays natural, setpts for video) and reassembles. That way I can set specific scenes to 2x/4x/5x/custom and hit my target submission runtime just by re-running the script — no re-recording, no cutting actual content.
```
```

```
```
6. POLISH
```
```
Animated intro/outro with real motion, not a zoom or crossfade. No staged results anywhere, no console errors in the footage.
```
```

```
```
Work through this on your own, don't ask me questions. Only pause for something that spends real money or a decision the codebase genuinely can't resolve.
```

title: Impeccable Autonomous Styling — Anti-Slop Pass
body:
Impeccable Autonomous Styling — Anti-Slop Pass
Uses Impeccable — the design-language skill/plugin for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI etc. (npx impeccable install, then /impeccable init). No placeholders — it installs itself if missing, reads the product to figure out its own design direction, and runs every relevant command across every surface until the slop detector comes back clean.
/goal Make this project's UI actually impeccable — install/use the
Impeccable skill, kill every AI-slop pattern, and give every surface a real
design point of view. Don't ask me for design direction, work it out
yourself.

1. GET IMPECCABLE RUNNING
   If it's not already installed, install it (`npx impeccable install`,
   tailored to whatever harness this is running in) and initialize it
   (`/impeccable init`). If it's already set up in this repo, use what's there.

2. LEARN THE PROJECT BEFORE TOUCHING ANYTHING
   Read the existing codebase for design tokens, components, and
   conventions — don't invent a new system if one already exists, inherit
   it. If there's no PRODUCT.md, write one yourself from the actual product:
   who uses it, what mode each surface is in (persuade / operate / read /
   experience), the brand voice, and explicit anti-references — the generic
   AI defaults this project should never look like (gradients, glassmorphism,
   italic serif hero, side-tab nav, nested cards, pulsing dots, generic
   drop shadows, numbered section labels, and so on). Infer all of this from
   the code, README, and copy already there — don't ask me for it.

3. HIT EVERY SURFACE, NOT JUST THE LANDING PAGE
   Walk every page/screen/component in the app and run whichever Impeccable
   commands actually fit that surface's job — `/impeccable audit`,
   `/impeccable polish`, `/impeccable typeset`, `/impeccable distill`,
   `/impeccable colorize`, `/impeccable layout`, `/impeccable adapt`,
   `/impeccable animate`, `/impeccable delight`. A dashboard and a landing
   page don't need the same treatment — use the mode you set in step 2 to
   decide what each surface actually needs.

4. BE ACTUALLY CREATIVE, NOT JUST SAFE
   Don't settle for "polished but generic." Commit to one real visual point
   of view for this product — a specific palette, type pairing, and layout
   language, consistent everywhere — instead of the first safe AI-default
   direction. If Impeccable's world/dice mechanic is available, use it to
   get pushed out of the model's own default taste rather than just tidying
   up what's already there.

5. PROVE IT'S CLEAN
   Run the detector (`npx impeccable detect src/`, or the equivalent hook)
   across the whole codebase. Anything it flags gets fixed for real, never
   suppressed or ignored. Loop fix → re-detect until it comes back with zero
   findings — not "mostly clean."

6. DOCUMENT IT SO IT STAYS CONSISTENT
   Run `/impeccable document` to write or update DESIGN.md so the system
   this run committed to is portable, and any later change — by you or
   another agent — inherits it instead of drifting back to generic defaults.

Keep moving through all of this in one continuous run — don't stop to show
me options or ask for design direction unless Impeccable genuinely can't be
installed or run in this environment. When it's done, tell me what visual
direction you committed to and why, which surfaces you touched, and confirm
the detector is clean.

title: Taste Skill Redesign — Audit-First, One Direction, Every Surface
body:
Taste Skill Redesign — Audit-First, One Direction, Every Surface
Uses Taste Skill (Leonxlnx/taste-skill) — the anti-slop skill suite for Cursor/Claude Code/Codex/etc. It's a suite, not one skill, so this prompt is deliberate about which pieces get used and why, rather than throwing all 13 at the project at once:
* taste-skill v2 (design-taste-frontend) — the core system. Does brief inference, picks a real design system or native CSS, dual-mode by default, and has the hard pre-flight check this prompt leans on.
* redesign-skill — audit-first protocol for existing projects, which is what this is. Runs before anything gets changed.
* soft-skill / minimalist-skill / brutalist-skill — the three visual directions. Only one gets used, chosen by brief inference, never blended.
* output-skill — stays on the whole run so nothing ships as a placeholder or half-finished section.
* stitch-skill — exports DESIGN.md at the end so the direction sticks.
* image-to-code-skill / imagegen-frontend-web — optional, only if a locked visual reference would help before implementing.
* gpt-tasteskill is deliberately skipped — that variant's tuned for GPT/Codex models, not relevant here. brandkit and imagegen-frontend-mobile aren't pulled in unless the project actually needs a brand kit or is mobile.
Fits the /goal character limit (~2,670 chars).
/goal Redesign this app's whole UI using Taste Skill — audit-first since it's an existing project, one committed visual direction, every surface, zero placeholders. Don't ask me for style direction, that's what the skill's brief inference is for.

PHASE 0 — INSTALL THE RIGHT SKILLS
Install taste-skill (`npx skills add Leonxlnx/taste-skill`) — gives you v2 (`design-taste-frontend`), redesign-skill, soft-skill, minimalist-skill, brutalist-skill, output-skill, stitch-skill, image-to-code-skill, imagegen-frontend-web/mobile, brandkit. Skip gpt-tasteskill — that variant's for GPT/Codex, not this agent. Keep output-skill active the whole run: no placeholders, no skipped sections, no half-finished work, anywhere.

PHASE 1 — AUDIT FIRST (redesign-skill)
This is an existing app, not a blank canvas. Before changing anything, audit every page/screen: what's genuinely working and should stay, what reads as generic or templated or AI slop. Follow v2's redesign protocol (§11) — preservation rules before modernization levers, don't rip out what's already good just to have changed something.

PHASE 2 — LET IT INFER THE DIRECTION, COMMIT TO ONE
Use v2's brief inference (§0) — industry, audience, mood, motion depth — to pick ONE coherent visual direction, then layer in exactly one of soft-skill (calm, expensive, soft contrast), minimalist-skill (editorial, restrained, sharp hierarchy), or brutalist-skill (Swiss, mechanical, raw structure) — whichever the brief actually calls for. Don't blend all three. If a locked visual reference would help before implementing, generate one first with imagegen-frontend-web (or -mobile), then build closely to it using image-to-code-skill's reference-first workflow.

PHASE 3 — IMPLEMENT ACROSS EVERY SURFACE
Apply the committed direction to every page and screen, not just the landing page. Dual-mode light/dark by default, real contrast and hierarchy parity across both (§8). Reach for a real component system (Material, Fluent, Carbon, Radix, shadcn, etc.) only where the brief actually calls for one, native CSS otherwise (§2) — don't default to a library just because it's familiar.

PHASE 4 — HARD PRE-FLIGHT CHECK
Before calling anything shipped, run the hard pre-flight check (§14) — every item has to honestly pass, not be assumed. Nothing gets marked done with a "TODO: style this" left behind.

PHASE 5 — DOCUMENT IT (stitch-skill)
Export DESIGN.md with stitch-skill so the direction committed to here doesn't drift on the next change.

Keep moving through this in one continuous run. Only pause if the pre-flight check genuinely can't pass without a decision only I can make.

title: Trading Research — Any Market, Fully Autonomous
body:
Trading Research — Any Market, Fully Autonomous
Same pipeline as before, but no symbol to fill in — Phase 0 is new and has it survey and pick its own markets (crypto, equities, forex, futures, whatever it can get real data for) instead of you naming one. Fits the /goal limit (~3,770 chars).
What else changed for the broader scope: testing many strategies across many markets raises the odds one looks good purely by chance (multiple comparisons), so Phase 3's bar now requires a strategy to hold up across more than one out-of-sample period, not just pass once — and Phase 6's report now includes the total count of strategies/markets tried, so you have the context to judge how much of a "win" could be luck.
The real-capital gate (Phase 6) is unchanged and non-negotiable: research, backtest, and paper forward-test run continuously on their own; nothing touches a real exchange account or places a real order without your explicit go-ahead.
/goal You are an elite quantitative trading researcher. Pick your own markets, run a continuous research loop discovering, backtesting, and forward-testing strategies across whatever's genuinely promising. Never connect to a real exchange account or place a real order without my explicit go-ahead.

PHASE 0 — PICK THE MARKETS YOURSELF
No fixed symbol. Survey candidates broadly — crypto pairs, equities, forex, futures, anything with real historical data and real paper-execution available — and choose which are actually worth researching: liquid, enough real history, genuinely tradeable. Note why each got picked. Rotate across several rather than fixating on one.

PHASE 1 — RESEARCH LOOP, PER MARKET
Each iteration, for whichever market you're on:
- Research real sources: academic papers, quant research, indicator docs, public trading communities. Note actual sources found — don't invent citations.
- Generate ONE new idea per iteration. Track every idea already tried, per market, in ideas.md and reject trivial parameter reshuffles (a new MA length on the same crossover isn't new) — genuinely different logic each time.
- Shell out to the Claude Code CLI as a sub-process for deeper research or heavier backtesting compute if it helps.

PHASE 2 — BUILD IT AS A REAL, BACKTESTABLE STRATEGY
Implement the idea as an actual TradingView (Pine Script) strategy — real entry/exit logic, real position sizing, real stop loss and take profit. If Pine Script doesn't fit this market, use a real backtest script (Python/vectorbt/backtrader/whatever's already in this repo) with the same rigor.

PHASE 3 — BACKTEST WITH REALISTIC ASSUMPTIONS, NO SHORTCUTS
- Real historical data, never synthetic or mocked candles.
- Real costs: fees, realistic slippage, a position size that wouldn't actually move that market's real order book.
- No look-ahead bias — only information genuinely available at each bar.
- Tune in-sample, then run once, unchanged, on out-of-sample data it never saw. In-sample-only performance is overfit, not profitable.
- Testing many strategies across many markets raises the odds something looks good by pure chance. One lucky out-of-sample pass doesn't qualify anything — require it to hold across more than one out-of-sample period.

Qualifies only if, across those periods: net profit > 0, genuinely positive risk-adjusted return (Sharpe/Sortino, not luck on a few trades), tolerable max drawdown, enough trades to be statistically meaningful.

PHASE 4 — LOG EVERYTHING, HONESTLY
Every strategy tried, every market, pass or fail: the idea, the market, the numbers, exactly why it passed or failed. Don't only keep winners — a log that hides failures isn't a research log.

PHASE 5 — FORWARD TEST QUALIFYING STRATEGIES (PAPER, NOT REAL CAPITAL)
Anything clearing Phase 3 runs forward on live/unseen data for that market, paper-traded — real data, real signals, real simulated fills, no real capital. Track performance over time, not one good stretch, logged the same honest way.

PHASE 6 — HUMAN GATE BEFORE ANY REAL CAPITAL
If a strategy holds up over a meaningful forward-test period, STOP. Report backtest, out-of-sample, and forward-test results together, plus total strategies and markets tried so I can judge how much could be chance. Wait for my explicit go-ahead before touching a real exchange account. Never place a real order or handle real API keys on your own initiative. State plainly that past performance isn't a guarantee of future results — as part of the finding, not a footnote.

Check in periodically with a status update — markets covered, strategies tried, anything promising. Keep looping through Phases 0-5 without asking permission between iterations. The only hard stop is Phase 6.
